chunk_findings.detail: The new `anchor = head_since if head_since is not None else start` applies the head-arrival reset to *all* wait limits, including an explicit `wait_s` passed from `ddflow ci run --timeout N`. That breaks the function’s own documented contract at line ~230 that the per-run override “bounds the queue wait too”. Concrete failure: with `wait_s=1` (via `--timeout 1`), a run queued at position 2 at `t=0` reaches the head at `t=0.9` and the slot stays busy until `t=1.5`. The new code uses `head_since=0.9`, so it does not time out at `t=1.0`; it can break and start the run at `t=1.5` (or later), exceeding the caller’s 1-second queue-wait bound. The default `suite_wait_s` bug fix should not silently relax the explicit per-run override in the process.

chunk_findings.detail: The same `wait` value is both `[ci].suite_wait_s` and the per-run `wait_s` override, and the new `anchor = head_since` restart applies to both. The docstring above still promises that `ddflow ci run --timeout N` bounds queue wait in either direction (Ba5d5d63f12). chunk_findings.detail: `_PYTEST_RUN` only treats `pytest`/`py.test` as a token when the character before it is start-of-string or one of whitespace, `;`, `/` is not included — the class is `[\s/;|&(]`, so a `/` does not count. chunk_findings.detail: A command is a “whole suite” whenever it contains a pytest token and names no test file. `pytest --version` and `pytest --help` match that, so `_runs_whole_suite` is true and `run_command_gate` still queues behind a foreign holder. chunk_findings.detail: The regression only asserts `_runs_whole_suite("true")` is false. It never holds the suite lock and calls `run_command_gate` on `true`. On the old code the predicate assertion fails, but a later change that still queues every `unit_tests` command regardless of `_runs_whole_suite` keeps this test green while `ddflow gate run … unit_tests` with `command = "true"` still waits as #3. chunk_findings.title: tests/test_gate_suite_lock.py:58

chunk_findings.detail: The new check only takes the suite lock when the command contains a literal `pytest`/`py.test` token. A `unit_tests` gate that runs the full suite through any other runner—for example `make test`, `./run_tests.sh`, `bazel test`, or `cargo test`—has no named test files, so `WK.count_test_files(...)` is `None`, but `_runs_pytest(...)` returns `False` and `_runs_whole_suite` returns `False`. Two concurrent `ddflow gate run` tasks with `[gate.unit_tests] command = "make test"` then both start at once instead of the second queuing behind the suite lock, so the host can be saturated or shared test artifacts can collide. This is a regression from the previous behavior, which treated any non-`ddflow ci` `unit_tests` command without named test files as a whole suite.
